title: Bài sưu tầm 106 - Passage 1: The Story of Tyrian Purple
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 106

The Story of Tyrian Purple

Paragraph 1. In the ancient Mediterranean world, long before the invention of synthetic pigments, colour was an unmistakable signifier of wealth, political power, and divine favor. None was more revered than Tyrian purple, a rich, non-fading dye named after the Phoenician coastal city of Tyre (modern-day Lebanon). Unlike terrestrial dyes derived from plant roots or crushed insects, this coveted pigment was harvested through a laborious maritime process using predatory sea snails, primarily belonging to the species Bolinus brandaris and Hexaplex trunculus.

Paragraph 2. The production of Tyrian purple was notoriously complex and repulsive. Snail populations were trapped along rocky coasts using baited wicker baskets submerged in deep water. Once hauled ashore, the snails’ tiny hypobranchial glands were meticulously punctured or excised with sharp knives. For smaller shells, workers crushed the entire organism. The extracted glandular fluids were steeped in salt brine for three days before being transferred into immense vats made of lead. These open vessels were simmered continuously over low wood fires for ten days. As the liquid slowly concentrated, organic matter was repeatedly skimmed from the surface. The stench generated by decomposing marine tissue was infamous; ancient writer Pliny the Elder recorded that the foul odour surrounding Phoenician dye works was detectable miles away, ensuring that factories were always relegated to the outermost perimeters of coastal settlements.

Paragraph 3. The transformation of the chemical precursor into a vibrant colour required photochemical oxidation. When first secreted by the molluscs, the fluid appeared completely clear. Exposure to ambient sunlight initiated a dramatic photochemical reaction, shifting the fluid gradually through shades of yellow and vivid green before finally stabilizing as a deep, lustrous purplish-crimson. Because the dye chemically bonded with textile fibres rather than merely coating them, fabrics coloured with Tyrian purple did not fade with laundering; instead, sun exposure and aging often made the hue darker and more brilliant.

Paragraph 4. The value of the dye was astronomical due to its minuscule yield: modern chemical reconstructions demonstrate that roughly 10,000 snails were sacrificed to produce just one single gram of pure dye powder. Consequently, purple fabric was worth its weight in silver or gold. In Imperial Rome, the pigment became an exclusive symbol of state authority. The Senate instituted strict sumptuary laws specifying exactly who could display the colour, reserving all-purple togas exclusively for the Emperor, while high-ranking magistrates were permitted only a narrow purple stripe on the hem of their robes. To maintain economic dominance, Roman authorities cracked down violently on merchants producing cheap counterfeit garments dyed with common madder root or kermes insects.

Paragraph 5. The decline of Tyrian purple was precipitated by geopolitical upheaval. Following the sack of Constantinople in 1204 and its ultimate fall in 1453, the Byzantine imperial workshops that maintained the closely guarded dye secrets ceased operations. Within decades, the intricate trade knowledge vanished from Mediterranean culture. It was not until 1856, when 18-year-old chemist William Henry Perkin accidentally synthesized mauveine while attempting to formulate an artificial cure for malaria, that purple clothing finally became accessible to ordinary citizens. Today, the scale of this lost ancient craft is attested by colossal mounds of discarded snail shells still visible along the Lebanese coastline, silent monuments to one of the ancient world’s most lucrative industries.

groups.title: Questions 8–13
groups.instructions:
Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 106?
In boxes 8–13 on your answer sheet, write:
TRUE – if the statement agrees with the information
FALSE – if the statement contradicts the information
NOT GIVEN – if there is no information on this

steps: Đoạn 2: "...trapped along rocky coasts using baited wicker baskets..." | Distractors: traps, vessels.
Từ cần điền: baskets.
Đoạn 2: "...transferred into immense vats made of lead." | Distractor: wood.
Từ cần điền: lead.
Đoạn 2: "The stench generated by decomposing marine tissue was infamous..." | Distractors: odour, matter.
Từ cần điền: stench.
Đoạn 3: "Exposure to ambient sunlight initiated a dramatic photochemical reaction..." | Distractor: sun.
Từ cần điền: sunlight.
Đoạn 4: "The Senate instituted strict sumptuary laws specifying exactly who could display the colour..." | Distractor: regulations.
Từ cần điền: laws.
Đoạn 4: "...dyed with common madder root or kermes insects." | Distractor: insects.
Từ cần điền: root.
Đoạn 5: "...attested by colossal mounds of discarded snail shells..." | Distractors: monuments, perimeters.
Từ cần điền: mounds.

q8.text: Tyrian purple gradually lost its colour intensity after repeated washing.

steps: Đoạn 3: "...did not fade with laundering; instead, sun exposure and aging often made the hue darker..." → Mâu thuẫn trực tiếp với gradually lost its colour intensity.
Kết luận: FALSE.

q9.text: Roman senators were allowed to wear togas made entirely of purple fabric.

steps: Đoạn 4: "...reserving all-purple togas exclusively for the Emperor, while high-ranking magistrates were permitted only a narrow purple stripe..." → Thượng nghị sĩ không được mặc nguyên cây màu tím.
Kết luận: FALSE.

q10.text: The recipe for making Tyrian purple was written down and circulated among Venetian merchants after 1453.

steps: Đoạn 5: "...the Byzantine imperial workshops... ceased operations. Within decades, the intricate trade knowledge vanished..." → Tri thức bị thất truyền, không hề được lưu hành cho thương nhân Venice.
Kết luận: FALSE.

q11.text: William Henry Perkin created mauveine during an intentional effort to synthesize an artificial textile dye.

steps: Đoạn 5: "...accidentally synthesized mauveine while attempting to formulate an artificial cure for malaria..." → Tìm thuốc trị sốt rét, không phải cố ý tổng hợp chất nhuộm vải.
Kết luận: FALSE.

q12.text: Modern researchers have successfully calculated the number of snails needed to create a given quantity of Tyrian purple.

steps: Đoạn 4: "...modern chemical reconstructions demonstrate that roughly 10,000 snails were sacrificed to produce just one single gram of pure dye powder."
Kết luận: TRUE.

q13.text: The Lebanese government has granted protected heritage status to ancient snail shell deposits.

steps: Đoạn 5: Có nhắc đến các bãi vỏ ốc khổng lồ dọc bờ biển Lebanon vẫn còn thấy ngày nay, nhưng không có thông tin chính phủ Lebanon có cấp quy chế bảo tồn di sản hay không.
Kết luận: NOT GIVEN.
